skills.name: Travel words and basic spelling rules

note.text:
Travel words: a journey (going from one place to another), the departure (leaving), the arrival (coming), the destination (the place you are going to), the timetable (the times of buses or trains), a passenger, the fare, a ticket, luggage, a delay (being late).
Spelling rules when we add an ending:
• A word ending in silent e drops the e before -ing: ride → riding, arrive → arriving (but not before -s: arrives).
• One short vowel + one consonant, stressed at the end: double it: stop → stopping, plan → planned. British English also doubles l: travel → travelling.
• Consonant + y changes y to i: carry → carries, carried; but vowel + y keeps the y: journey → journeys, delay → delayed.
• A word ending in -ie changes ie to y before -ing: lie → lying.

worked_example.problem: Add -ing to {a} and {b}, and write the plural of {c}.
steps: {a} ends in one vowel + l: British English doubles the l: {ing(a)}.
{b} ends in a silent e: drop the e: {ing(b)}.
{c} ends in a vowel + y: keep the y and add s: {plural(c)}.

cards.idea: The words of a journey: you leave at the departure time and reach your destination at the arrival time.
example: Departure: seven o'clock, from Buea. Destination: Bamenda.
Arrival: two o'clock. A delay means the bus is late.

cards.idea: Drop a silent e before -ing: ride → riding.

check.prompt: Write the -ing form of the verb.

cards.idea: Double the last consonant after one short stressed vowel: stop → stopping, plan → planned. British English doubles l too: travel → travelling.
Consonant + y: change y to i before -es or -ed. Vowel + y: keep the y.

questions.prompt: Match each travel word to its meaning.

the time a bus, train or plane comes in
the place you are travelling to
a list of the times buses or trains leave and arrive

questions.prompt: Write the -ing form of the verb.

misconceptions.explain: Double the last consonant after one short stressed vowel: {ing(v)}.

e: Consonant + y: change y to i and add -es.
Change the y to i: carries.

pick.s: The bus was ___ by the rain.
e: Vowel + y: keep the y and add -ed.
Add -ed: delayed.

pick.s: We made two long ___ last year.
e: Vowel + y: keep the y and add s.
Just add s: journeys.

pick.s: My mother ___ about the late bus.
e: Consonant + y: change y to i and add -es.
Change the y to i: worries.

pick.s: She ___ at her aunt's house every holiday.
e: Vowel + y: keep the y: stays.
Just add s: stays.

pick.s: The children ___ to catch the bus.
e: Consonant + y: change y to i before -ed.
Keep the i: hurried.

pick.s: Our ___ is Kribi: that is where we are going.
e: Departure is leaving.
The fare is the money you pay.

pick.s: Check the ___ to see when the next train leaves.
e: Luggage is bags.
A passenger is a traveller.

pick.s: There was a long ___ because of an accident on the road.
e: Arrival is coming in.
A ticket shows you have paid.

pick.s: The ___ of the plane is at 10:30, so we must be at the airport by nine.
e: The destination is the place you go to.
The journey is the whole trip.

pick.s: Put your ___ under the seat, please.
e: The fare is money.
A timetable is a list of times.

questions.prompt: One word is spelt wrongly. Which sentence has it?

wrong.explain: British English, used in Cameroon, doubles the l: travelling.
Drop the silent e before -ing: arriving.
Vowel + y keeps the y: journeys.

wrong.text: The driver stoped at the checkpoint.
